description:
Approved by the user 2026-11-17 (GC session, BEAM comparison on bench, fz develop vs BEAM 28.3). Profile first.
Evidence: survive costs 1503 ns per KB copied vs BEAM's 126. Workloads that copy a lot cost 333-436 ns/KB on fz vs 83-300 on BEAM.
Hypothesis, unverified: each collection frees about 205 MB of off-heap binaries, with two free() calls per binary.

comments.text: Profiled on develop 4a05ae2be + experiment probe (branch exp/gc-clock in ../fz-gcclock: Instant timers around Heap::collect phases and shared_bin_destructor_heap; never merge). survive, 3 runs: GC 28-36 ms; Cheney scan 6.7-9.4 ms, off-heap sweep 19.6-27.9 ms, block release <0.01 ms. 200,001 binary destructors take 18.3-20.8 ms (about 95-105 ns each, timer overhead included) = nearly the whole sweep. Each binary is <<n::64, pad::binary>> of 1024 bytes, freed as two allocations (buffer + 48-byte SharedBin box, bits.rs shared_bin_destructor_heap). Telemetry: the 31 collections visit 0 stubs until the last three (major 75,995, minors 55,994 and 57,995), so the cost lands in three collections. So survive's 1.5 us/KB copied is not copying: about two-thirds of its GC time is freeing binaries. Not yet verified: what BEAM pays for the same 200k frees (its whole GC is 2.9 ms); next probe is BEAM's sweep cost and a one-allocation binary (header and bytes together, as BEAM's Binary). Other phases for reference: enum scan 52 of 55 ms; msg 106,062 collections, scan 3.6 + sweep 2.0 + release 10-12 of 40-49 ms, the rest is per-collection fixed cost (~250 ns each), which is fz-9x7.7's subject.

Leak A/B (probe branch exp/gc-clock 8a2452976-based, build-time FZ_PROBE_LEAK makes shared_bin_destructor_heap return without freeing; own staticlib per arm, md5s differ), survive, 7 interleaved runs each, local M-series: instructions median 1,694.2M (free) vs 1,633.4M (leak) = 60.8M fewer = ~304 instructions per destroyed binary (200,001 destroyed); cycles median 428.8M vs 368.7M = 60.1M = ~300 cycles per binary, 14% of the whole program's cycles. Each destruction is two system-malloc frees (1025-byte buffer, 48-byte SharedBin box) plus the Box reconstruction. Timer-based sweep figures were too noisy on this run to use; the counters are the evidence. Candidate fixes, to be proposed: (1) one allocation per SharedBin (header followed by its bytes), halving frees and dropping a pointer chase; (2) fz-9x7.22's allocator round answers how much is system malloc's per-free cost - survive should be one of its workloads, with this leak arm as the floor.

title: Find what makes survive's collections cost 1.5 µs per KB copied
